Hi Olga,

Thanks for the demo last week — BrightSpark is excited to proceed. Procurement asked me to share a draft PO and a couple points we need you to confirm before we loop Legal for signatures: 

- We have a staggered committed spend request (minimum-commit staircase) across 12 months. Can Redwood support a payment ladder rather than a single prepaid min-commit?
- Our AP prefers Net-60 for SaaS vendors. Can Redwood accept Net-60 for hosted API invoicing? If not, can we do Net-45 for committed capacity?
- We operate through an EU subsidiary for invoicing (BrightSpark Labs EU S.à r.l.). Can Redwood invoice the EU entity to avoid VAT reverse-charge headaches, or will Redwood require US invoicing and customer VAT handling?
- Please confirm how taxes/VAT will be represented on invoices and whether Redwood will include gross-up language.

Attached: BrightSpark_PO_draft.pdf (PO with the staircase amounts).

If you can propose simple language we can pass to our legal team (one page), that’d speed things up. Can we aim to finalize order form redlines this week?

Thanks — appreciate it.

— Emma

From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>

Emma — thanks for the note and the PO. Quick responses below, then I’ll loop in finance/legal for redlines: 

- Payment ladder: Redwood can support a staged minimum-commit schedule on the Order Form ("commitment staircase"). Typical pattern we use for customers is 50% initial invoice upon signature, 25% at month 3, 25% at month 6 for the first tranche. We can map your 12-month staircase to that approach or align invoices to your requested milestone dates.

- Net terms: Our hosted default is Net-30. For committed capacity we have flexibility — we can move to Net-45 for the committed tranche with Finance approval. Net-60 is unusual for us, but if this is a hard requirement we can evaluate with a credit review and possibly require an escrow or ACH pre-funding for the first tranche.

- Invoice entity / VAT: Redwood prefers to invoice the contracting entity on the Order Form. If BrightSpark can accept invoices from the EU subsidiary, we can bill the EU entity and avoid a US/VAT mismatch. If you need Redwood to invoice a US entity and BrightSpark handles the VAT, we’ll include tax line items as provided by our tax team.

- Gross-up: we don’t include automatic gross-up language by default. For EU invoicing we typically reflect VAT separately; for US invoicing we show applicable sales taxes. If there is a GST/VAT withholding situation, we’ll need to capture the certificate/evidence up front.

Attaching our current order form template so legal can mark up: redwood_standard_orderform_v4.docx. Looping in Marissa (Legal) and Ben (Finance) on next steps.

Proposed next step: Marissa to provide redline + short clause language; Ben to confirm whether Net-45 is approvable and what credit/escrow conditions (if any) apply.

Olga

Olga / Ben / Karthik — reviewed. High-level position below and suggested redline snippets you can forward back to BrightSpark. I kept language narrow to avoid MSA churn.

1) Commitment staircase / invoicing: we can accept a multi-tranche minimum-commit schedule. Add clause to Order Form: 
"Customer may phase Minimum Commitment across defined instalments. Redwood will invoice each instalment according to the schedule in Appendix A. Failure to pay an instalment is a breach allowing Redwood to suspend services after 14 days' notice."

2) Net terms: Finance confirmed Net-45 for committed capacity is acceptable with two conditions: (a) Redwood issues the first invoice (50%) on signature and requires payment within Net-30; (b) subsequent tranche invoices may be Net-45. For Net-60 we would require a credit review and one of: a refundable deposit equal to the first tranche, or an escrow arrangement. Add a short clause referencing a credit approval process.

3) Invoice entity & VAT: we should allow the customer to nominate an invoice entity on the Order Form (contracting party). Add fields for invoicing entity name, tax ID, and jurisdiction. Include: 
"Customer must provide valid VAT registration or tax residency documentation prior to the first invoice for non-US entities. If Customer requests Redwood to invoice an affiliate, Customer will ensure timely payment and provide indemnity for any tax/withholding obligations."

4) Tax gross-up: we should avoid unconditional gross-up. Instead add a tax-handling clause: 
"Invoices will list taxes separately. Customer is responsible for any taxes, duties or withholdings imposed on payments unless otherwise required by law. If withholding applies, Customer must provide supporting evidence to qualify for reduction or exemption."

5) Security for extended terms: for deals > $1,000,000 total committed ARR, Finance proposes either an escrow or pre-funded first tranche. If BrightSpark's staircase is below that, standard Net-45 is fine.

I attached a one-page redline (redline_orderform_BSL.docx) you can send to the customer. I also recommend we include a sample invoice template to reduce back-and-forth (Finance can produce).

If you want, Ben can include the sample invoice and the credit checklist in the response.

— Marissa
